_meta.doc: App registry built by scripts/build_apps.py from cua_gym_apps.json + gym_anything_apps.json + apps/*.md. Never hand-edit.

amendments.by: catalogue port of the five hub apps hub_apps() could not admit
amendments.why: The upstream importer read native_state_keys out of each clone's own SCHEMA.md by matching markdown table rows. The four added apps ship no SCHEMA.md at all, so they got no row; google_analytics_mock and youtube_mock write their state as a fenced code block instead of a table, so they got state_keys: []. All six serve the hub contract and five of them have a pinned schema document in catalogs/app_schemas. state_keys here is derived from that document by hub_app.top_level_keys, the reader validate_state uses.
amendments.note: These bytes are no longer the imported bytes; manifest.json pins them as amended, not as provenance. Rebuilding from scripts/build_apps.py in the source repository would drop them.

amendments.by: catalogue port of the last five hub apps hub_apps() could not admit
amendments.why: All five always served the hub contract and all five already had a row. Four carried schema: "" because scripts/build_apps.py admits an apps/*.md document only when it has both a state-schema section and an "Observable State Changes" table, and none of these four upstream documents has the second one -- a documentation gap, not a reason the app cannot be seeded. youtube_mock carried state_keys: [] because its clone writes the state as a fenced code block rather than a markdown table, so the row-matching importer read nothing. The four documents are imported byte-for-byte (two from CUA-Gym/.claude/skills/mock_websites/schemas, two from the clone's own SCHEMA.md), the provenance the other 94 have, and each was checked against the state the app itself posts: zero drift on all five (experiments/interact/drift-20260910).
amendments.state_keys: hub_app.top_level_keys of the pinned document, the reader validate_state uses. This replaces flattened lists that mixed top-level and nested names (195 entries for TradingView, 167 for wandb, 15 for tripadvisor, 10 for westlaw); every top-level name in the old lists survives.
amendments.note: These bytes are no longer the imported bytes; manifest.json pins them as amended, not as provenance. Rebuilding from scripts/build_apps.py in the source repository would drop them.
